review.summary:
Phase 7 ("Experimental and export closure") is implemented to a high standard and its acceptance criteria are met with evidence I could independently trace to code and recorded executions, not prose.

Export closure is real. `tools/native_exports.py` reconciles all 3,820 frozen capabilities (2,630 roots + 1,190 members) against concrete public Rust paths, source files, named test functions and explicit deliberate differences, and refuses to emit a ledger when any row is unresolved (`main()` raises on `gaps`), when a mapped native method is absent, when a probe does not textually reference its claimed path, or when frozen provenance/denominators drift. The 13 adversarial tests in `tools/test_native_exports.py` exercise exactly those rejections (root omission, deferred model fallback, pending operation, unrelated probe, path traversal/symlink evidence). Closure is then proved twice: a generated in-repo probe test and a genuinely separate Cargo package (`contracts/native-probes`) compiled and executed on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 with PANW/AIRS/SCM environment stripped (`docs/checks/phase-07-native-exports-1.89.0.json` → `passed: true`, exit 0, musl host recorded).

The four Phase 7 workstreams are substantive, not stubs. AgentGuard implements all four frozen read methods with correct dual data/management planes, OAuth-only auth, derived `x-tsg-id`, pre-auth query validation and the observed `time_period=30_DAYS` default, with 6 contract tests. Realtime is a careful implementation: exact RFC 6455 accept digest comparison, rejection of redirects, duplicate critical headers, unsolicited extensions/subprotocols, bounded 64 KiB/128-header upgrade, `catch_unwind` around the third-party framer, sensitive headers, no global crypto-provider mutation, latched errors, deterministic drop ownership and a bounded close — covered by 14 tests across `realtime_contracts.rs` and `native_realtime.rs` (the latter against a real loopback TCP server with hand-built frames). `provision` implements an explicit stage/scope/workspace/cleanup state machine that never deletes a possibly-referenced scope after an ambiguous write, with 8 tests hitting precisely those branches. Helper/constant/configuration/error equivalents are verified against a real frozen-TypeScript oracle (`tools/helper-oracle.mts` loads the baseline modules with network stubbed and env cleared; 157 cases and 163 constants asserted in `helpers_contracts.rs`), including JS-semantics details like `js_trim`, UTF-16 length limits, `ryu_js` number formatting and `toLowerCase` of U+0130.

Every one of the ~40 gate commands in `commands_for(7)` is present in `docs/checks/phase-07.json` with exit code 0, `passed: true`, `source_unchanged: true`, and `source_sha256` equal to the reviewed source SHA. Documentation is unusually candid about what is not proved (no live acceptance, musl-only native execution, CI not yet updated).

What keeps this from a 10 is one genuine defect in the phase's own generated artifact plus some evidence-binding and tidiness gaps, detailed below. None of them is a security or functional gap in library code, and none invalidates the recorded evidence.

findings.description: The generated probe test's crate-level gate is `#![cfg(all(feature="scan", "management", "gateway", "model-security", "red-team", "realtime"))]`, but the file body references `scm_sdk::airs::agentguard::AgentGuardClient` and its four methods (lines 110-128), which are `#[cfg(feature = "agentguard")]` in crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/agentguard/mod.rs:5-8. `agentguard` is not implied by any gated feature (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:24). Building with exactly the declared set, e.g. `cargo test --no-default-features --features scan,management,gateway,model-security,red-team,realtime`, therefore fails to compile the test target with an unresolved path. The recorded matrix never hits this: default/minimal leave the gate off and `--all-features` turns agentguard on, so the escape is real but untested. The ledger already computes the correct answer (`requiredFeatures: ["agentguard"]` via feature_for()), so the gate is simply not derived from it.
findings.required_fix: In tools/native_exports.py:425, derive the emitted `#![cfg(all(...))]` list from the union of `row["requiredFeatures"]` across all capabilities instead of hardcoding six features (at minimum add `feature = "agentguard"`), regenerate contracts/native-exports.json and crates/scm-sdk/tests/native_export_probes.rs, and add a recorded check running `scripts/check-rust.py` for the exact probe feature set so the gate cannot drift again.

findings.description: The CI matrix still pins `toolchain: ['1.88.0', '1.99.0']` while this phase raised the workspace minimum to `rust-version = "1.89"` (Cargo.toml:7) for patched tokio-websockets 0.13.3. The 1.88.0 jobs can no longer resolve the workspace. docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:101 discloses this honestly and assigns the CI update to Phase 8, and no remote run is claimed as evidence, so it is disclosed rather than hidden; it is nonetheless a known-broken configuration introduced by this phase and a one-line fix.
findings.required_fix: Update the matrix toolchain to `['1.89.0', '1.99.0']` (and the docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:101 note) so the committed workflow matches the declared minimum, leaving actual retained remote execution as the Phase 8 obligation.

findings.description: `GatewayRealtimeOptions::max_buffered_events` is a public field that is only range-checked in `validate()` (lines 166) and never used to bound anything, because the implementation keeps no SDK event queue. docs/REALTIME.md:28-30 states this plainly, but the field itself carries no rustdoc, so a consumer reading the generated API docs would reasonably believe it bounds a queue. This is the closest thing in the phase to an inert knob relative to the "no placeholder methods or unsupported aliases" criterion.
findings.required_fix: Add a rustdoc comment on `max_buffered_events` stating that the native implementation has no SDK event queue and that the value is validated as a bound the zero-queue implementation trivially satisfies (mirroring docs/REALTIME.md), or remove the field and record the removal as a deliberate difference.

findings.description: 45 ledger rows bind only `crates/scm-sdk/tests/native_export_probes.rs::all_public_export_paths_compile` as test evidence. These are facade namespace accessors such as `AIGatewayClient`, `AIGatewayClient.configs`, `.apiKeys`, `.auditLogs`, `.adminGuardrails`. The accessors are in fact exercised behaviorally (22 call sites across crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_contracts.rs and management_contracts.rs), so this is an under-citation in the ledger rather than a coverage hole, but it means these rows' recorded proof is compile-only.
findings.required_fix: Extend the class/accessor branch in tools/native_exports.py (lines 332-347, 385-392) to bind the owning family's contract test functions when the accessor is used by them, so the 45 facade rows cite executed behavioral evidence instead of only the compile probe.

findings.description: The RFC 4122 UUID predicate is re-implemented inline (36 chars, dashes at 8/13/18/23, hex elsewhere) and is byte-for-byte identical to crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/scan/scanner.rs:193 `is_uuid`, with equivalent copies in airs/gateway/common.rs:93, airs/management/mod.rs:121, airs/red_team/common.rs:55 and airs/model_security/mod.rs:41. Each copy sits behind a different feature, which explains the duplication, but six copies of a frozen validation rule is a maintenance hazard: a future correction must be applied in six places.
findings.required_fix: Move the predicate to a feature-independent location (e.g. crates/scm-sdk/src/data.rs or a small `validation::is_uuid`) and have the per-product `uuid()` wrappers and the AgentGuard check call it, keeping their existing error kinds.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-07.json: source_sha256 921ab15afd82841ec23a8e8780b808898e774eae87e50aa476f9d717a4a96080 matches the reviewed source state, source_unchanged true, passed true; all ~40 recorded commands have exit_code 0 and verbatim stdout/stderr.

Recorded command set matches tools/check_phase.py:114-137 commands_for(7) in order, including the 1.88.0→1.89.0 MSRV substitution, python tools/native_operations.py --check --require-through-phase 7, tools/native_exports.py --check, test_native_exports.py, scripts/check-native-exports.py for 1.89.0 and 1.99.0, and scripts/check-rust.py for agentguard/realtime/ws-transport.

python tools/native_exports.py --check printed {"checked": true, "frozenRoots": 2630, "frozenCapabilities": 3820, "implemented": 3820, "unresolved": 0, "liveVerified": 0}; tools/native_exports.py:499-500 raises when any gap exists, so 0 unresolved is enforced rather than asserted.

scripts/check-native-exports.py compiled and ran the standalone contracts/native-probes package offline on two toolchains; docs/checks/phase-07-native-exports-1.89.0.json records passed true, sourceUnchanged true, frozenCapabilities 3820, exit_code 0, rustc 1.89.0 host x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, with an explicit limitation that this proves public API probes and literal assertions, not live workflows.

tools/test_native_exports.py: 13 adversarial tests passed, including test_root_omission_cannot_shrink_the_frozen_denominator, test_unrelated_probe_cannot_claim_an_api, test_removed_concrete_method_is_rejected_before_rust_compilation, test_pending_operation_is_reported_as_a_gap, test_deferred_model_is_never_hidden_by_a_generic_type_fallback, and test_evidence_paths_reject_absolute_paths_traversal_and_symlinks.

tools/helper-oracle.mts:14-55 executes tools/verify-contracts.py against .local/typescript, deletes all process env, stubs fetch/WebSocket to throw, imports the frozen baseline modules and records their actual outputs; --check reported {"checked":true,"cases":157,"constants":163}. crates/scm-sdk/tests/helpers_contracts.rs:403-427 and 894-914 assert exactly 163 constants and 157 cases against that fixture, including expected-failure cases.

crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/agentguard/client.rs implements all four frozen methods on the correct planes against .local/typescript/src/agentguard/client.ts (GET /v1/scans, /v1/stats/scans with 30_DAYS default, /v1/scans/{uuid}/vulnerabilities, management /v1/rules); crates/scm-sdk/tests/agentguard_contracts.rs contains 6 tests covering planes/headers/order/defaults, pre-auth validation, malformed responses, constructor admission and deadline/cancellation.

crates/scm-sdk/src/realtime/native.rs:255-342 validate_upgrade enforces HTTP/1.1, status 101, single Upgrade/Connection/Sec-WebSocket-Accept, exact canonical SHA-1 accept digest, and rejects extensions/subprotocols/Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding; its unit tests assert the RFC 6455 known vector and that oversized/duplicate/bad-accept responses never panic. crates/scm-sdk/tests/native_realtime.rs adds 6 loopback tests for masking, ping/pong, fragmented unicode tails, retained pre-framing bytes, invalid UTF-8/binary, ping floods and unconfirmed close.

crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/gateway/provision.rs:286-304 skips scope deletion whenever the workspace create outcome is Unknown or the scope was caller-owned, and records ProvisionScopeState/ProvisionWorkspaceState/ProvisionCleanup separately; crates/scm-sdk/tests/gateway_provision_contracts.rs has 8 tests including ambiguous_creations_never_replay_or_delete_a_potential_dependency and binding_failure_keeps_confirmed_workspace_receipt_for_explicit_recovery.

crates/scm-sdk/src/configuration.rs and environment.rs replace the JS mutable singleton (.local/typescript/src/configuration.ts:113) with per-instance state and explicit zeroized bounded env snapshots; crates/scm-sdk/tests/configuration_contracts.rs has 8 tests including atomic failed reinitialization, js_trim/blank suppression parity, OAuth precedence and retry clamping, and child-process capture plus non-UTF-8 handling.

The Phase 2 open parity item oauth-token-buffer-configuration is closed: crates/scm-sdk/src/auth.rs:43-60 adds RefreshBuffer::Fixed for exact tokenBufferMs equivalence alongside the safer Adaptive default, matching .local/typescript/src/management/oauth-client.ts:38,105.

scripts/check-package.py recorded archive_sha256 f9a0c2ec…, 793753 bytes, and a file list that includes src/airs/agentguard/*, src/airs/gateway/provision.rs, src/realtime/*, src/configuration.rs, src/constants.rs, src/environment.rs, src/helpers.rs, src/error/problem.rs and examples/realtime.rs, confirming the new Phase 7 surface is actually packaged and compiles as a consumer crate under 1.89.0.
limitations: I could not recompute any SHA-256 digest. The reviewed-source digest and the docs/checks/phase-07.json digest given in the prompt, and the internal sourceBindings/probe hashes in contracts/native-exports.json, are taken as stated; I verified only that docs/phase-status.json and docs/checks/phase-07.json record the same source_sha256 value as the prompt.

Tools were read-only: I did not execute any check, test, cargo command or generator. All pass/fail conclusions rest on the verbatim stdout/stderr/exit codes preserved in docs/checks/phase-07*.json, plus my own reading of the code and tests those commands run.

The agentguard feature-gate defect is a static analysis conclusion (probe body references a `#[cfg(feature = "agentguard")]` item that the file's own gate does not require). I could not compile the offending feature combination to confirm the exact rustc error.

No live service acceptance exists for any Phase 7 capability; phase-status records live_acceptance as pending_phase_8 and docs/EXPORTS.md, docs/REALTIME.md and docs/AGENTGUARD.md state this explicitly. I judged implementation and offline contract evidence only.

Native execution evidence covers only x86_64-unknown-linux-musl, and the native WebSocket adapter is additionally restricted to 64-bit targets by a compile_error in realtime/native.rs:23-26. Other declared platforms remain unqualified (a Phase 2 limitation already deferred to Phase 8).

Compile probes establish that each mapped public path exists, is public and type-checks; they do not establish behavior. Behavioral assurance comes from the separate contract suites, which I sampled (helpers, constants, agentguard, realtime, provision, configuration) rather than read exhaustively across all 3,820 rows.
I did not inspect credential or tenant-registration files, and I read .local/typescript only as the frozen nonsecret baseline reference.
